Canonical form of a set of identifiers, and whether two sets agree

Source: R/identifiers_scope.R
canonical_identifiers.Rd

canonical_identifiers() completes ids with the session's value of every key it lacks (fill), recording those keys in attr(, "assumed"): a key an object does not store is read from the session, so it is compared as the session's value too. Keys that are not identifiers (e.g. from an older object) are left out and named in attr(, "unknown"). Given data, it also resolves an identifier that lists alternative columns (e.g. barcode = c("Barcode", "Plate")) to the one present, so two objects built the same way store the same identifiers.

Usage

canonical_identifiers(ids, data = NULL, fill = get_env_identifiers())

same_identifiers(a, b)

Arguments

ids, a, b

named lists of identifiers.

data

optional data.frame, or character vector of column names, the identifiers describe.

fill

named list giving the value of a key ids lacks. Defaults to the session's identifiers.

Value

canonical_identifiers(): a named list over every identifier key. same_identifiers(): a flag.

Details

same_identifiers() is TRUE when two sets name the same columns. A key resolved to one column agrees with a list of alternatives that contains it, and lists of alternatives or tags (barcode, template, untreated_tag) are compared as sets; well_position keeps its order. The keys that differ are in attr(, "differ").

Examples

ids <- canonical_identifiers(list(barcode = c("Barcode", "Plate")), data = "Plate")
ids$barcode # "Plate"
#> [1] "Plate"
attr(ids, "assumed")
#>  [1] "duration"                     "cellline"                    
#>  [3] "cellline_name"                "cellline_tissue"             
#>  [5] "cellline_ref_div_time"        "cellline_parental_identifier"
#>  [7] "cellline_subtype"             "drug"                        
#>  [9] "drug_name"                    "drug_moa"                    
#> [11] "untreated_tag"                "masked_tag"                  
#> [13] "well_position"                "concentration"               
#> [15] "template"                     "drug2"                       
#> [17] "drug_name2"                   "drug_moa2"                   
#> [19] "concentration2"               "drug3"                       
#> [21] "drug_name3"                   "drug_moa3"                   
#> [23] "concentration3"               "data_source"                 
#> [25] "replicate"                    "normalization_type"          
same_identifiers(list(barcode = "Plate"), get_default_identifiers())
#> [1] TRUE
#> attr(,"differ")
#> character(0)
